{{short description|Field extension of algebraic number field characterized by prime ideals of inertial deg 1}}
{{redirect|Bauer's theorem|the theorem in perturbation theory|Bauer–Fike theorem}}
In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[algebraic number theory]], a '''Bauerian extension''' is a [[field extension]] of an [[algebraic number field]] which is characterized by the [[prime ideal]]s with [[inertial degree]] one in the extension.

For a finite [[Degree of a field extension|degree]] extension ''L''/''K'' of an algebraic number field ''K'' we define ''P''(''L''/''K'') to be the set of primes '''p''' of ''K'' which have a factor '''P''' with inertial degree one (that is, the [[residue field]] of '''P''' has the same order as the residue field of '''p''').

'''Bauer's theorem''' states that if ''M''/''K'' is a finite degree [[Galois extension]], then ''P''(''M''/''K'') ⊇ ''P''(''L''/''K'') if and only if ''M'' ⊆ ''L''.  In particular, finite degree Galois extensions ''N'' of ''K'' are characterised by set of prime ideals which split completely in ''N''.

An extension ''F''/''K'' is ''Bauerian'' if it obeys Bauer's theorem: that is, for every finite extension ''L'' of ''K'', we have ''P''(''F''/''K'') ⊇ ''P''(''L''/''K'') if and only if ''L'' contains a subfield ''K''-isomorphic to ''F''.

All field extensions of degree at most 4 over '''Q''' are Bauerian.<ref name=Nark416>Narkiewicz (1990) p.416</ref>
An example of a non-Bauerian extension is the Galois extension of '''Q''' by the roots of 2''x''<sup>5</sup> − 32''x'' + 1, which has Galois group ''S''<sub>5</sub>.<ref name=Nark394>Narkiewicz (1990) p.394</ref>
